chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb and Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah and Dhubyān ibn Ḥakīm, from Mūsā ibn Ukayl al-Numayrī, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayyābah, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

“There is no harm in placing the deceased between your legs and standing over him to wash him. When you turn him to the right and the left, you hold him steady with your legs so that he does not fall onto his face.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: Practice is according to what we mentioned earlier, namely that the one washing does not mount the deceased, and that is what is preferable. This report is to be understood as indicating permissibility and the lifting of prohibition, even though something else is preferable.

key_terms.الْغَاسِلُ: the person performing the washing of the deceased
key_terms.الْمَيِّتَ: the deceased person being prepared and washed
key_terms.شِمَالًا: to the left side while turning the body
key_terms.فَتُغَسِّلَهُ: to wash him as part of the funerary ghusl
key_terms.يَمِينًا: to the right side while turning the body

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to stand over or brace the deceased with one’s legs while performing ghusl on the body?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the manner of washing the deceased and indicates that stabilizing the body with one’s legs while turning it during ghusl is permissible. Shaykh al-Ṭūsī clarifies that although this is allowed, the preferred practice is that the washer should not mount or sit upon the deceased.
